This turns each off-critical zeta zero into a pole of the prime–polar continuation with residue proportional to its multiplicity.

declarations.name: canonicalNegativeEulerSheet_divisor_polarity

declarations.name: windowObservable_no_limit

declarations.name: riemannZeta_eq_zero_iff_echoLadder

declarations.name: tendsto_boundaryChart_escape
declarations.doc: `(24)`: the divisor charge escapes every compact boundary chart.** In the boundary coordinate `z = L(s-1)` the branch point attached to a zeta zero `ρ ≠ 1` runs off to infinity at speed `log N`.

declarations.name: deriv_riemannZeta_line_eq_zero_iff_deriv_hardyZ_of_zero

declarations.name: not_mem_closedSpan_of_continuous_evaluation

declarations.name: exists_terminalHardyPhase_finiteCertificateZeroLaw

declarations.name: exp_theta_mul_deriv_riemannZeta_line_eq_deriv_hardyZ_of_zero

declarations.name: tendsto_unitRieszCoefficientResidue
declarations.doc: Equation (17).** The continued coefficient transform keeps a genuine pole at every nontrivial zeta zero, with residue `3 m / (2 rho (rho + 1/2))`: the probability multiplier vanishes to first order there, but the logarithmic-derivative pole survives.

declarations.name: deriv_riemannZeta_eq_zero_iff_thetaCuspFirstSineMoment_of_zero

declarations.name: analyticOrderAt_coPoissonCancelledSource_eq_pred_of_mellin_ne_zero

declarations.name: primeGradeMonodromy_zero_residue
declarations.doc: (3)–(4) The grade-one prime monodromy at a strip zero.** At every zeta zero to the right of the critical line the continued grade-one source has residue exactly minus the multiplicity: the higher prime-power grades are holomorphic there.

declarations.name: jetSymbol_vanishing_of_analyticOrder
declarations.doc: The Jordan multiplier hierarchy.** At a zeta zero of multiplicity `m` the symbol of the `k`-th lift vanishes exactly for `k < m`, so the mode annihilated by every lower lift is exposed by the `m`-th one.

declarations.doc: Zeta-zero reflection off the two pole ladders.** The zero locus of `ζ` is invariant under `s ↦ 1 - s` on the whole plane minus the even ladder `-2m` and its reflection `1 + 2m`.

declarations.name: reflCocycle_zeta_eq_ite
declarations.doc: Unconditional open-strip zeta cocycle normal form.** The totalized reflection cocycle of `ζ` is the archimedean Gamma ratio off the zeta zero locus and is zero exactly on that locus. This is the sharp replacement for externally assuming `ζ(s) ≠ 0`.

declarations.name: reflCocycle_zeta

declarations.doc: A `HasSum` representation over `ℂ` automatically gives absolute summability of the Gaussian envelopes. This uses finite dimensionality of `ℂ` over `ℝ`; it removes the need to import a separate zeta zero-counting estimate merely to dominate the detector tail.

declarations.name: primeBoundary_monodromy_charge
declarations.doc: `(22)`: the quantized monodromy charge.** At every zeta zero to the right of the critical line, the continued prime-log current has a simple pole whose residue is exactly the zero's multiplicity; equivalently the continued prime zeta function has a logarithmic branch point of charge `m_ρ` there.

declarations.name: dyadic_or_triadic_polarCoefficient_not_squareSummable_at_zero
declarations.doc: The fixed literal dyadic and triadic rational-interval windows jointly exclude ordinary `H₀`: at every positive-real-part completed-zeta zero, at least one exact polar coefficient is not square summable. No window is selected from the zero divisor.

declarations.name: half_le_norm_detPolyC
declarations.doc: The detection lower bound.** If the mollified Euler–Maclaurin remainder at a zeta zero is at most `1/2`, the detection polynomial has modulus at least `1/2` there. This is the analytic input a zero-density argument consumes: a zero of `ζ` becomes a large value of an explicit finite Dirichlet polynomial.

No boundary avoidance premise remains in the conclusion.

declarations.doc: The regular reciprocal is analytic wherever the entire zeta residue unit is nonzero.

declarations.name: zetaResidueUnit_ne_zero_of_ofReal_pos
declarations.doc: The entire zeta residue unit has no zero anywhere on the positive real axis.

declarations.doc: The zero-counting bound.** The zeros of `ζ` within `1/8` of `9/8 + iγ`, counted with multiplicity, number `O(log|γ|)`.

declarations.name: visibleCoprimeZetaMixedJet_re_pos_of_half_lt_re
declarations.doc: Right of the critical line the visible-coprime zero jet is strictly positive.

declarations.name: bdTarget_dist_floor
declarations.doc: The quantitative floor at a point of the right half-plane.** Every element of the carrier annihilated by the detector at `ρ` stays at distance at least `√(2Re ρ − 1)/|ρ|` from the target. No property of `ρ` beyond `½ < Re ρ` is used: the zeta zero enters only through `bdTarget_dist_floor_of_mem_closedSpan`, which identifies a set of annihilated vectors.

declarations.name: exists_wide_zero_count
declarations.doc: The zero count on the wide disc.** Any family of zeros in the disc, satisfying Landau's inequality at the centre, has size `O(log|γ|)`.

declarations.name: riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_re_gt_one_sub
declarations.doc: The de la Vallée Poussin zero-free region**: `ζ(β+it) ≠ 0` for `|t| ≥ 9` and `β > 1 − c/log⁹|t|`.

declarations.name: PcalObservable_no_limit_of_amplitude_ne
declarations.doc: Tent genuine pole from a nonvanishing amplitude.** For a nontrivial zeta zero `ρ` (`ρ ≠ 1`, `Re ρ > 0`, `ρ ≠ ½`) with `A_L(ρ-½) ≠ 0`, the tent observable `PcalObservable L` has no finite limit at `s = ρ + ½` — a genuine pole. The polar and correction terms are continuous there (the correction via the widened `HL` holomorphy), so the pole is inherited entirely from the prime channel (`windowObservable_no_limit`).

declarations.name: logDeriv_riemannZeta_add_reflect_of_one_lt_re
declarations.doc: Reflection formula in the half-plane of absolute convergence.** Both nonvanishing hypotheses are discharged there: `ζ(s) ≠ 0` classically for `Re s > 1`, and `ζ(1-s) ≠ 0` because reflection preserves the zeta zero locus off the two pole ladders. What remains is the arithmetic condition that `1 - s` avoid the trivial zeros, i.e. that `s` not be an odd integer `1, 3, 5, …`.

declarations.name: offcritical_residue
declarations.doc: Off-critical residue / divisor tomography** (§5, eqs. 24–25). Each zeta zero `ρ` with `Re ρ > 1/2` (`ρ ≠ 1`) produces a genuine simple pole of the prime term at `s = ρ + ½`, with residue `2·m(ρ)·A_L(ρ-½)²` — nonzero because `m(ρ) ≥ 1` and the rectangular amplitude does not vanish in the open right half-plane (`rectangularWindowAmplitude_ne_zero`). So no off-critical pole cancels, and the residue reads off the exact analytic multiplicity `m(ρ)`.

declarations.name: logDeriv_residue_of_factorization
declarations.doc: Residue of a logarithmic derivative at a zero equals the multiplicity.** If, near `ρ`, an analytic function factors as `f = (z-ρ)ⁿ·g` with `g` analytic and `g(ρ) ≠ 0`, then `(s-ρ)·(f'/f)(s) → n` as `s → ρ`. For a genuine zero `n ≥ 1`; the residue of `-f'/f` is then `-n`. This is the local structure that turns a zeta zero of order `m` into a pole of `-ζ'/ζ` with residue `-m`.

declarations.name: norm_riemannZeta_le_of_zero
declarations.doc: Mean value from a zero**: if `ζ(β+it) = 0`, the value at `σ'+it` is bounded by `112·log²|t|·(σ'−β)` along the segment inside the derivative-growth region.

declarations.name: artin_stark_simpleZero_order_classifier
declarations.doc: Stark simple-zero order classification.** Let `degree i` be positive character degrees and `order i` the integer orders of corresponding Artin L-functions at a fixed point. If the Artin--Takagi weighted order is `1` and Foote--Murty square norm is at most `1`, then exactly one component has degree and order both `1`; all other orders vanish. In particular, no component has a pole. This is dependency-closed arithmetic core of literature's simple Dedekind-zeta-zero case.

declarations.name: expIntegralE1_le_exp_neg_div
declarations.doc: The Jensen loss.** `E₁(x) ≤ e^{−x}/x` for `x > 0`: the Gaussian log-mean `E₁(1/σ²)` is exponentially smaller than the Jensen bound `log(1+σ²) ≈ σ²`.

declarations.name: polarPrimeObservable_no_limit
declarations.doc: General genuine pole of the renormalized observable.** At a zeta zero `ρ ≠ 1`, if the window `W` is continuous with `W(ρ+½) ≠ 0`, then `polarPrimeObservable κ W` has no finite limit at `s = ρ+½`: the polar counterterm `κ·ζ(s-½)` is continuous there (`ρ ≠ 1`), so the prime channel's simple pole survives. This closed meromorphic form carries no error term, so the statement holds on the whole plane with no strip restriction — the detection primitive for two-width divisor recovery.

declarations.name: tent_twoWidth_divisor_recovery
declarations.doc: Tent two-width complete divisor recovery.** For irrationally related widths `L₁, L₂`, every nontrivial zeta zero `ρ` (`ρ ≠ 1`, `Re ρ > 0`, `ρ ≠ ½`) — critical-line ones included — is a genuine pole of at least one of the two tent observables `PcalObservable L₁`, `PcalObservable L₂` at `s = ρ + ½`. A single width can miss a critical-line zero where its amplitude `A_L(iγ)` vanishes, but incommensurable widths never share such a zero (`sharpAmplitude_not_both_zero`), so the joint pole divisor of the two observables is the entire nontrivial zeta divisor.

declarations.name: sharpObservable_twoWidth_divisor_recovery
declarations.doc: Sharp-window two-width complete divisor recovery.** For irrationally related widths `L₁, L₂`, every nontrivial zeta zero `ρ` (`ρ ≠ 1`, `ρ ≠ ½`) — critical-line ones included — is a genuine pole of at least one of the two renormalized sharp observables `polarPrimeObservable (4α) (-2·A_L(s-1))` at `s = ρ+½`. The sharp window `A_L(s-1)` is linear, so its poles are simple with residue `∝ A_L(ρ-½)`; incommensurable widths never share an amplitude zero (`sharpAmplitude_not_both_zero`), so the joint pole divisor is the entire nontrivial zeta divisor. Cleaner than the tent version: the closed meromorphic form needs no error-term holomorphy, hence no strip restriction (`Re ρ > 0` not required).

declarations.name: HL_differentiableOn_gt_half
declarations.doc: Holomorphy of `H_L` on the maximal strip `{Re s > ½} ∖ {1}`.** The weighted error series `∑_k (Λ(k)/√k)·E_{k,L}(s)` converges absolutely and locally uniformly wherever the dominating von Mangoldt series `∑ Λ(k) k^{-σ-½}` converges, i.e. `σ > ½` — the full half-plane `Re s > ½`, not just the Euler region `Re s > 1`. The single point `s = 1` is removed because the leading integral identity `∫ g_s = A_L(s-1)²` (hence `E_kL_bound_explicit`) is proved off the amplitude's removable singularity at `s = 1`; the ball around each `s₀ ≠ 1` is shrunk to avoid it. This is the strip in which every nontrivial-zeta-zero pole `s = ρ + ½` (including the critical-line heights `s = 1 + iγ`, `γ ≠ 0`) lives.

declarations.name: rh_sensitivity_threshold
declarations.doc: The Riemann hypothesis is a statement at the `σ = 1/2` scale of the prime measure.** For every `β` strictly between `1/2` and `1` and every `ε > 0` there is a positive generalized-prime density `g = adjoinedDensity β γ` on `(0, ∞)` such that `g ≥ 0`, and its `σ`-mass is `log (1 + γ²/(σ-β)²)` for every `σ > β`; its abscissa is exactly `β`: the `β`-mass diverges; its reciprocal mass — the total mass `∫ u⁻¹ dν(u)` of the adjoined generalized primes, which also bounds the shift of the Mertens sum — is smaller than `ε`; the adjoined Euler factor is `((s-β)² + γ²)/(s-β)²` on `Re s > β`; the enlarged zeta function `ζ(s)((s-β)²+γ²)/(s-β)²` vanishes at `β + iγ`, a point of the open half plane `Re s > 1/2`. Together with `zeros_unchanged_of_mass_abscissa_le_half` this localizes exactly which scale of a prime measure the Riemann hypothesis can see: an adjoined measure with abscissa at most `1/2` moves no zero, while an adjoined measure of arbitrarily small reciprocal mass and abscissa `β > 1/2` puts a zeta zero on the line `Re s = β`. No functional of a prime system that is continuous for the reciprocal (Mertens) mass can therefore decide the Riemann hypothesis.
